@graph.name: cat-harness-tools-schemas
@graph.description: Tests of cat-harness's schemas that exercise tools code: the sixteen `cat-harness/schemas/*.test.ts` files that imported `scripts/`, `src/`, `pipeline/` or `test/support/`, moved first (bean `70lx`, batch B0) so that no later batch of the code move leaves a harness file importing into this layer. Since bean `8lcl` (owner, 2026-10-30, card "A. One coordinated move") the Zod sources live here too: every `cat-harness/schemas/**/*.ts`, so this directory is the schema corpus and is typed `schemas` as well as `code`. cat-harness keeps the schemas that are data: the per-skill JSON Schemas in `schemas/skills/`, `staging-comparison.schema.json` and the PlantUML model.

@graph.name: cat-harness-tools-scripts
@graph.description: Scripts this layer runs. Holds `lib/roots.ts`, the one place that names the three roots a moved file can mean (HARNESS_ROOT, TOOLS_ROOT, REPO_ROOT), and its test; the harness's own `scripts/` arrives here batch by batch in the code move (bean `70lx`). Also the identifier lookup's pair, moved here from large-datasets when it dissolved into cat-harness (bean `j7ql`, 2026-10-01; D1: code goes to cat-harness-tools): `gen-id-lookup.ts` builds the prefix-sharded lookup over a catalogue's REFERENCED nodes for every instance that declares an `id-lookup` directory, and writes it THERE (`bun run cat id-lookup`, gated by `id-lookup:check`); `bench-id-lookup.ts` measures it at full catalogue scale on a seeded synthetic corpus (bean `4pm8`). Neither names a corpus: both read the checkout's declarations. And `extract-assets.ts`, the tool behind the harness's `asset-extraction` skill: a container's INDEX into a `folio-extraction/v1` record, moved down from `folio-assistant-core/scripts/` with its contract `cat-harness/schemas/content/extraction.ts` (bean `tlat`, placement PR5, owner ruling 2 of 2026-09-30).

@graph.name: cat-harness-tools-id-lookup
@graph.description: The identifier-lookup CLIENT a reader's browser runs: `lookup.js` (plain ES module, no dependencies) with its hand-written `lookup.d.ts`, and a one-form `index.html` told which index to open by `?index=<directory>`. The indexes themselves are generated output hosted by the instance each is about (its own `id-lookup/`), never here. JavaScript, so it never sits under the plain docs pipeline. Moved from large-datasets (bean `j7ql`).

@graph.name: cat-harness-tools-python
@graph.description: The Python toolchain's dependency manifests: `requirements.txt` (the LEAN set CI installs, `pip install -r cat-harness-tools/python/requirements.txt` from the checkout root) and `requirements-extended.txt` (declared, deliberately not installed in CI — its cost is stated per entry). @graph.name: cat-harness-tools-libraries
@graph.title: Software libraries
@graph.description: The outside libraries this layer's code imports: one `software-library/1.0.0` node per dependency in `package.json`, with the version and sha512 that `bun.lock` pins, the registry tarball, the SPDX licence read from the installed package, the range, whether it is a dev dependency, the files that import it (`usedBy`) and the `types/*.d.ts` shim that types it (bpmn-moddle, dmn-moddle). GENERATED, never hand-edited: `bun run cat libraries:derive` writes it and `libraries:check` fails on a stale node, an import no node names, and a shim no node names. The kind is cat-harness's (bean `jbvi`, option D: one outside-software core shared with `tool-release`); this layer keeps its own nodes because it pins its own versions. `held/<layer>/` holds the nodes of each layer below the kind, which may not name it (bootstrap-tools): `software-library/1.2.0` with `layer` naming the layer it describes, derived at this layer's pins (owner, 2026-10-30, bootstrap-tools#44).

@graph.name: cat-harness-tools-upstream
@graph.description: This layer's pinned-upstream registry, `upstream-pins.json` (`"$schema": "folio-upstream-pins/v1"`). It has one row for each upstream dependency whose pin literal is in a file this layer holds. Today that is only the pdf.js viewer, pinned in `scripts/pdf-viewer.ts`. Each row names the file the pin is READ from (`pinnedIn`, resolved against this instance's root), the pattern that reads it, and what of ours binds to the dependency. It holds no version. `bun run cat check:upstream-pins` reads it together with cat-harness's `upstream/` registry (`cat-harness-upstream`), which keeps the rows whose files are in the harness. It is a separate registry because a harness row naming a file in this layer is a wrong-direction reference (folio-assistant#1481). `code`: the checker's input table, not content any reader renders.

@graph.name: health
@graph.description: Repository health reports for THIS repository: the one `health-report/v1` document `bun run cat-harness-tools/test/health/run.ts --instance <this instance>` writes. Each repository the separation made is its own clone, with its own size, publish branch, branches and stores, so each carries its own report (owner, 2026-10-10: "All repos need health check").
